items.title: Counters
items.summary: One verified quantity becoming the focal event. Nine clean, high-contrast designs accelerate from a starting value to a final value, then hold long enough for the audience to register the magnitude.
items.usageRule: Select one counter design for one verified magnitude. Several designs may be sequenced only when the narration presents distinct sourced values; do not invent intermediate values to fill the animation.

useWhen: A single exact number is the point of the sentence.
A percentage, currency total, count, change, record, or cumulative magnitude needs visual emphasis.
A short assertion benefits from an accelerating count before holding on the final value.
requiredAssets: Unit, currency symbol, or percentage suffix
Short label or caption only when the chosen design includes one

timing.rule: Choose a scene for visual fit first, then calculate playback rate from native usable duration and the narration target duration. Preserve the native render and create a retimed derivative.

transitions.rule: Use the scene transition flags when selecting an isolated clip. Add a transition when needsTransition is true; do not treat unknown as confirmed.

avoidWhen: Multiple entities must be compared simultaneously.
The number is speculative or unsourced.
A document or chart must be inspected as evidence.

items.title: Photo Slideshow — Memories
items.abstractName: Tabletop print stack with peel reveals
items.summary: Handled photographs. Prints sit in angled stacks on a dark surface and are peeled away one by one to expose the next, or presented as pairs and rows. It communicates that these images belong together and are being looked through by someone.
items.tone: Warm, tactile, affectionate; a memory box.
items.usageRule: Choose for a short warm montage of personal photographs where a physical, handled quality is wanted and no captions are needed.

useWhen: Personal photographs in either orientation
Pairs and trios that belong together
Images with a clear central subject

usageMode.label: Individual scenes
usageMode.rule: Select scenes individually; check the chosen scene’s visible assets and transition status.

timing.rule: Choose a scene for visual fit first, then calculate playback rate from native usable duration and the narration target duration. Preserve the native render and create a retimed derivative.

transitions.rule: Use the scene transition flags when selecting an isolated clip. Add a transition when needsTransition is true; do not treat unknown as confirmed.

avoidWhen: Captions, names or dates are required
A neutral or contemporary register is required
The peel scenes would be used in isolation
Long segments: total run is 60 seconds

evidence.basis: Visually mapped scene change, refined using 8 fps motion samples; overlapping transition handles

items.title: Two-subject score comparison
items.capacity: 2 subjects; 9 shared metrics
items.visualEncoding: Portraits identify subjects; aligned text compares metrics. Body size does not encode a value.
examples: Two artists across sales, streams and awards
items.caveats: Supply winner flags from an explicit higher/lower-is-better rule; mixed units belong on separately labeled rows.

items.title: Two-panel trend comparison
items.capacity: 2 panels; 8 observations per panel; 2 series per observation
items.visualEncoding: Two lines per panel; the renderer also computes the mean difference between the two series.
examples: Catalog vs new-release streams across periods
avoidWhen: irregular time gaps interpreted as elapsed-time spacing
items.caveats: Category positions are equally spaced. Fixed y bounds apply; use the same units for both series and verify the meaning of the mean difference.

items.title: Full-body magnitude comparison
items.capacity: 3 subjects; 1 magnitude and 2 display labels each
items.visualEncoding: Bottom-aligned full-body height communicates magnitude; the native height formula is affine, not a zero-based ratio scale.
examples: Career record sales using full-body artists
avoidWhen: exact ratio claims from unconverted measurement values
items.caveats: For sales, explicitly map raw values to proportional target heights and invert the native calibration. A 38-to-1 ratio makes the smaller portrait tiny. Three slots remain fixed; never invent a third subject just to fill the layout.

items.title: Long chronological ledger
items.capacity: 40 entries arranged in 3 display columns: 13 / 13 / 14
items.visualEncoding: Text-led chronological lookup; column placement wraps the sequence and does not encode magnitude.
avoidWhen: a chart requiring visible proportional differences
items.caveats: Keep all 40 records and the measured column groups. One entry per displayed period; distinguish repeated people from distinct records.

items.title: Annotated outlier scatter
items.capacity: 14 points; 2 numeric variables each; 5 named callout slots
items.visualEncoding: Position on two numeric axes shows association; callouts focus attention on selected points.
items.caveats: Native bounds are x 25–50 and y 50–66. Five points have fixed callout positions; label values must agree with the plotted data and units.

items.title: Period-by-period leaders
items.capacity: 12 period rows; existing support for up to 3 leaders per period
items.visualEncoding: A categorical timeline of winners, including ties; portrait size is not magnitude.
avoidWhen: More than three leaders in a period
items.caveats: This existing optional-slot behavior is preserved, not a new resizing feature. Supply one image per populated leader and preserve all 12 period rows.

items.title: Equal-weight identity grid
items.capacity: 30 identity cells in 3 rows
items.visualEncoding: Equal marks show membership or coverage; no numerical variable controls size.
items.caveats: There is no numeric measure field in the active layout. Images remain in the current portrait/cutout treatment; arbitrary logos need separate media testing.

items.title: Two-cohort ranked lists
items.capacity: 2 lists of 10 entries each
items.visualEncoding: Two adjacent ordered lists compare the same measure across cohorts.
examples: Top ten album launches in two eras
avoidWhen: Different units or unmatched ranking criteria between lists
items.caveats: Sort each cohort deliberately. Structural era keys remain fixed even when editable display headings are changed.

items.title: Photo-led head-to-head metrics
items.capacity: 2 subjects; 6 shared metrics
items.visualEncoding: Two large contextual photos flank six text comparisons.
items.caveats: Use contextual photos with suitable upper-body framing. Winner emphasis must reflect the chosen metric direction.

items.title: Quotes with supporting score columns
items.capacity: 2 quote blocks; 3 value columns with 6 / 6 / 7 entries
items.visualEncoding: Large quotations frame compact numeric evidence; text has no proportional scale.
examples: Two artist claims with supporting career statistics
items.caveats: Quotes require accurate attribution in the supplied copy. Columns have unequal fixed capacities; do not imply matching row pairs where none exist.

items.title: Ranked table with aligned bars
items.capacity: 20 entries; 3 measures per entry; primary measure also charted
items.visualEncoding: Text supports precise lookup while bars compare the primary measure.
examples: Twenty artists by annual average output plus totals and tenure
avoidWhen: Primary values outside the fixed chart
items.caveats: The chart uses a fixed maximum of 10. Keep the table order aligned with bars; each supplied portrait appears in both the table and the chart. The first bar has fixed accent emphasis.

items.title: Recognition ledger and value profile
items.capacity: 2 lists of 10 entries; 1 plotted measure plus contextual fields
items.visualEncoding: An area profile over ordered entities accompanies two ledgers; the numeric field can represent age, tenure or another continuous measure.
items.caveats: Native plotted range is 18–50. Award symbols cap at five; do not represent larger counts solely with those symbols. The x axis is entity order, not elapsed time.

items.title: Single-subject introduction
items.capacity: 1 full-body subject; title and subtitle
items.visualEncoding: Large figure and typography create an introduction; no numeric scale.
items.caveats: No metric is required. Preserve a clean full-body cutout with enough resolution for the hero placement.

items.title: Four editorial photo cards
items.capacity: 4 subjects; 1 stamp/caption per card
items.visualEncoding: Equal photographic cards communicate a curated set or shared status.
examples: four leaders during a defining era
avoidWhen: A numeric ranking inferred from card size
items.caveats: Use photos suited to the existing crops. Stamps are editorial labels, not calculated ratings.

items.title: Single-subject annotated value
items.capacity: 1 full-body subject; 1 value callout
items.visualEncoding: A ruler-like callout emphasizes a stated value; portrait height itself is fixed.
avoidWhen: Comparing quantities by the person's rendered height
items.caveats: This is a label-driven fact card, not a data-scaled silhouette. Make the unit and meaning explicit so ruler styling does not imply physical stature.

items.title: Dense portrait scatter
items.capacity: 30 entities; 2 numeric variables each
items.visualEncoding: Portrait position on two axes communicates a relationship.
items.caveats: Native bounds are x 0–1600 and y 32–60. Close points can overlap; preview crowded clusters and keep a consistent measurement period.

items.title: Long bar history with threshold
items.capacity: 64 ordered periods; 1 measure per period
items.visualEncoding: Vertical bars show changes across a long sequence against a threshold.
examples: quarterly average score over sixteen years
avoidWhen: Raw ratio comparison from bar height
items.caveats: Native y range is 16–40, with a truncated baseline at 16 and threshold 20. Labels are evenly spaced periods; bar heights do not represent ratios of raw values.

items.title: Hero with chronological ledger
items.capacity: 1 hero; 18 period-value entries
items.visualEncoding: A full-body hero anchors a compact period-by-period list.
items.caveats: Keep the hero identity consistent across the ledger and any fixed highlighted entry; highlights are not a substitute for verifying the maximum.

items.title: One subject across two conditions
items.capacity: 1 full-body subject; 2 conditions; 8 paired metrics
items.visualEncoding: Mirrored text comparisons around one person emphasize change without scaling the body.
examples: An artist before and after signing
a founder before and after expansion
items.caveats: Use the same unit and definition within each pair. Time periods can instead be scenarios if clearly labeled as scenarios.

items.title: Subject ranking with peer context
items.capacity: 1 hero with 8 ranking fields; 3 peer callouts
items.visualEncoding: A dominant subject, ranking list and supporting peer context explain standing.
examples: Artist's eight category ranks with three benchmarks
items.caveats: The hero is intentionally dominant in size. Peer callouts and ranks must be supplied and sourced; portrait size is not rank magnitude.

items.title: Three multi-metric subject cards
items.capacity: 3 subjects; 6 metrics and 1 footer each
items.visualEncoding: Full-body cards offer side-by-side text comparisons with equal visual roles.
avoidWhen: One metric needing proportional body sizes
items.caveats: Metric labels and units must match across cards. Images are identity cues, not numeric encodings.

items.title: Compact portrait bar leaderboard
items.capacity: 30 entities; 1 measure each
items.visualEncoding: Dense horizontal bars compare a single quantity.
items.caveats: Fixed x maximum is 300. Inspect the configured threshold and ranking order; dense rows require short names and sufficient reading time.

items.title: Summary panel with portrait scatter
items.capacity: 4 summary rows; 8 plotted entities; 2 coordinates per plotted entity
items.visualEncoding: Text summaries accompany an eight-point scatter; summary rows are not additional points.
examples: Four era summaries beside eight artist positions
avoidWhen: Treating all twelve CSV rows as plotted entities
items.caveats: Both coordinates are mapped against 0–100. Studio currently requests 12 image assignments but only the last eight are plotted; extra input requirements remain unchanged. Some summary wording is fixed in the renderer.

items.title: Full-body portraits inside magnitude bars
items.capacity: 5 entities; 1 positive measure each
items.visualEncoding: Bars scale to the largest supplied value but have an 80-pixel minimum height.
avoidWhen: Exact large-ratio comparisons with tiny values
items.caveats: Bar height = max(80, value / maximum × 770). The minimum distorts low ratios; use a different template or future scale adaptation when exact ratios matter.

items.title: Two-group bar comparison
items.capacity: 2 groups of 5 bars; 4 header portraits per group
items.visualEncoding: Paired vertical bar charts compare two cohorts on a shared labeled scale.
examples: Five accomplishments in each of two artist collectives
avoidWhen: assuming ten inputs mean ten visible portraits
items.caveats: Eight portraits are drawn although Studio requests ten image assignments. Native ticks span 0–60, and minimum bar heights and per-slot reference calibration can override bar geometry for matching sample values; inspect proportional accuracy before making ratio claims. Some title/badge text is outside current Studio settings.

items.title: Fifteen portrait metric cells
items.capacity: 15 entities in a 5 × 3 matrix; 1 metric each
items.visualEncoding: A compact portrait matrix with numerical labels; size does not encode the value.
items.caveats: Use one consistently defined measure and denominator if it is a percentage. Color and portrait framing follow the fixed design.

items.title: Four framed portrait values
items.capacity: 4 entities; 1 displayed value each
items.visualEncoding: Four framed portrait cards compare text values using equal image treatment.
items.caveats: The existing card arrangement remains fixed. Any absent general title must be supplied through currently available captions, not an invented field.

items.title: Full-body lineup with context figure
items.capacity: 6 full-body figures; first 5 have period and value labels; sixth is a context figure
items.visualEncoding: A shared baseline creates a lineup; figure sizes are fixed stylistic placements.
examples: Five career stages beside a reference person
five artists plus a contextual host
avoidWhen: interpreting body sizes as sales ratios
items.caveats: The sixth figure has no active value/period fields. Portrait sizes do not automatically track the supplied values.

items.title: Seven pairwise outcomes with hero
items.capacity: 7 pairwise rows; 2 values and 2 portraits each; 1 additional hero
items.visualEncoding: Repeated head-to-head rows create an outcome narrative around a featured person.
examples: Seven chart battles involving a featured artist
items.caveats: Outcome badges and emphasis are fixed design elements. Verify they agree with the supplied results; 15 image assignments represent fourteen pair positions plus one hero.

items.title: Three five-member groups
items.capacity: 3 groups of 5 people
items.visualEncoding: Three labeled bands communicate membership or tier placement.
examples: three generations of five influential artists
items.caveats: Only names and portraits are active person data. Any tier or rank meaning must be backed by an explicit selection rule.

items.title: Two full-body profiles with eight metrics
items.capacity: 2 subjects; 8 shared metrics and 1 period label each
items.visualEncoding: Two large full-body figures frame aligned numeric comparisons.
items.caveats: Portrait sizes are decorative. Align units, reference dates and metric definitions across the two columns.

items.title: Five portrait headline values
items.capacity: 5 subjects; 1 value each
items.visualEncoding: Five headshots with prominent numbers create a simple comparison.
avoidWhen: a chart that must show numerical proportions
items.caveats: Numbers communicate magnitude; headshot size does not. Label common units clearly in the title.

items.title: Fifteen-entry portrait ranking
items.capacity: 15 entries arranged as 3 columns of 5
items.visualEncoding: Numbered positions and text values encode order; portrait size stays fixed.
avoidWhen: An unordered set presented as ranked
items.caveats: Sort the data before rendering and state the ranking criterion. Fixed rank labels follow positions, not a sorting operation.

items.title: Seven-tier portrait classification
items.capacity: 27 subjects across 7 tiers: 1 / 2 / 5 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 4
items.visualEncoding: Stacked bands show ordinal membership; neither within-tier spacing nor portrait size is a numerical score.
items.caveats: Keep the fixed tier membership counts. Provide evidence-based criteria and replace inherited tier captions; the renderer does not classify people for you.

items.title: Three criteria tables with benchmarks
items.capacity: 3 tables of 10 entries; mark and score per entry; 2 hero portraits
items.visualEncoding: Three compact tables expose component scores alongside featured subjects.
avoidWhen: Assuming the renderer computes similarity or validates scoring weights
items.caveats: Marks, scores, benchmarks and weights are supplied. Document the method and do not claim appearance implies character or other unmeasured traits.

items.title: Two criteria tables with benchmarks
items.capacity: 2 tables containing 12 and 10 entries; 2 hero portraits
items.visualEncoding: Two unequal tables summarize two scoring dimensions.
avoidWhen: Equal row-by-row pairing across both tables when entities differ
items.caveats: Both table sizes are fixed and unequal. All evaluations are precomputed inputs, not automated judgments.

items.title: Candidate scores with visible criteria
items.capacity: 10 candidates; 1 score each; 6 criteria captions; 1 hero
items.visualEncoding: A ranking table beside a prominent reference person explains a supplied assessment.
examples: Ten artists compared with a musical benchmark
ten applicants compared on documented requirements
items.caveats: The six criteria are captions, not six separate numeric inputs. Compute scores outside the renderer and disclose their basis.

items.title: Ascending score bars with benchmarks
items.capacity: 35 entries; 1 numeric score each; 2 hero portraits
items.visualEncoding: Ascending zero-based bars show a distribution of scores.

items.title: Receding rank ladder with photographic bodies
items.capacity: 1 measured magnitude per entity; 35 entities as shipped, ~12–40 workable; 1 hero cutout required, 1 optional cutout per remaining entity; no on-screen text except one authored number.
items.visualEncoding: Vertical position encodes the magnitude on a linear scale rescaled between the smallest and largest supplied values. Depth encodes evenly spaced rank order and is not magnitude. Marker size is a compressive restatement of vertical position and is then cancelled by perspective, so apparent size is not a value. Marker width follows the source image's aspect ratio and is not a value. Marker tilt, colour, fog and exposure are decorative. The dashed benchmark line and the vertical beam are correctly placed from data; the number printed beside them is a fixed authored string and is not computed.
examples: Top-40 revenue by division with the runner-up as the named benchmark
career totals across a ranked field of athletes, performers or researchers
annual output by plant or facility where one site dominates
vote totals in a multi-candidate contest with a decisive leader
population by city with the largest city measured against the second
avoidWhen: the smallest value is a large fraction of the largest
on-screen names, values, axes or a legend are needed
two or more independent variables must be shown
several entities are near-tied at the top
items.caveats: Nothing quantitative is legible in this layout. showAnnotations is false and the clean-cinema stylesheet hides every HTML overlay, so the only text rendered anywhere is the lead-guide sprite — whose value is a literal string in the layout definition and does not change when the data changes. The vertical axis floors at the minimum supplied value, not at zero, and no tick reveals this. Depth spacing is uniform regardless of value gaps. As shipped, 34 of the 35 markers show unrelated stock cutouts assigned by array index.

items.title: Particle relief over a ranked field
items.capacity: 1 measured magnitude per entity; 35 entities as shipped, ~20–60 workable; the 18,000-particle surface is generated regardless of entity count; 1 optional hero portrait; no axis or tick labels are rendered.
items.visualEncoding: Vertical position of the 35 micro-markers encodes log10 of the magnitude and is truthful. The particle relief is a generated Gaussian field whose peaks SUM where entities are close together, so surface height is not a value and does not preserve rank order. Particle colour is a height ramp and is not a category. Depth position is not a value. Marker size restates vertical position. Fog, grain, stars, glow and auto-orbit are decorative. Nothing in the scene is geographic.
examples: the shape of a distribution across a large ranked population — where the mass sits, whether it is bottom-heavy
density of activity across an ordered index, as an establishing or transitional shot
an atmospheric backdrop for narration that names magnitudes verbally while the field is shown as a field
cluster or crowding impressions in a population where individual identity does not matter
avoidWhen: The claim is about who is highest, or by how much
the axes would be read as places, maps or terrain
any entity must be individually identified
peaks would be counted, compared or measured
values must be read off the scene
items.caveats: This layout's own callout is false as rendered. It asserts 'HIGHEST PEAK · 59.5M · Drake forms the dominant terrain summit', but the surface is a sum of overlapping Gaussian bumps and the largest entity's peak is only the 9th highest of 35 — the tallest surface point belongs to an entity with under a third of the maximum value. Rank correlation between value and rendered peak height is roughly 0.74, not 1.0. Separately, the depth axis labelled 'ERA DEPTH' is a sine wave of the array index with no data behind it, and this was never disclosed to the project owner. The 35 micro-markers ARE positioned truthfully; only the surface and the depth axis are not.

items.title: Radial instrument stage with light-node magnitudes
items.capacity: 1 measured magnitude per entity; 35 entities as shipped, ~15–60 workable; 1 optional hero portrait; a value-tier legend renders and is valid; no axis or tick labels are rendered.
items.visualEncoding: Node height and the length of the stem beneath it encode log10 of the magnitude and are readable. Radius encodes rank in evenly spaced steps and is not magnitude. Angular position is not a value. Node colour encodes the entity's value tier and matches the legend. Node size restates height. The disc, the three concentric rings, the 72 instrument ticks and the five echo points around each node are decorative and are not concentric with the data. Additive blending means overlapping nodes look brighter, and brightness is not a value.
examples: a ranked population spanning several orders of magnitude, shown as a single field with one summit
an instrument-panel establishing shot for a segment about measurement, monitoring or a sensor network
a roster of contributors, stations, sites or products where the leader should read as the outermost, tallest signal
an audience, output or citation distribution where the log spread is the honest reading
avoidWhen: Angular position or clock position would be read as meaning
the story is the size of a gap rather than an ordering
several entities must be individually identified on screen
any entity has a zero, negative or missing value
a benchmark line or a two-way comparison is needed
items.caveats: Radius is rank, not value: the step from the smallest entity to the second smallest is exactly the same distance as the step from the runner-up to the leader. Stem length is proportional to the log difference from the smallest entity in the set, so the shipped 959× value spread renders as a 23.5× stem-length spread. The decorative rings and ticks are centred on the world origin while the data spiral is centred about 0.5–0.6 world units away, so a node's apparent ring membership is off. Unlike the Terrain Cloud layout, this layout's shipped callout is accurate for the shipped data — the largest entity does occupy the highest node.

items.title: Two-portrait qualitative comparison on a photographic stage
items.capacity: 0 measured dimensions — this layout encodes no data at all. Exactly 2 portrait subjects, 1 background plate, 1 three-line heading, 5 comparison word-rows, 2 kickers, 2 footers and 1 note. Observations are required by the loader and are never rendered.
items.visualEncoding: Nothing in this scene encodes a quantity. Left and right position separate two subjects and are not a value. Portrait height, portrait size and portrait placement are authored constants and are not values. Colour, light, fog and the curved backdrop are decorative. The five comparison rows are word pairs, not measurements, and the scene prints 'CONCEPT COPY · REPLACE WITH VERIFIED STORY DATA' beneath them. There are no axes, no ticks, no legend readout, no markers and no numbers anywhere in the frame.
examples: one subject before and after a defining event, era or transformation
two competing organisations, strategies, doctrines or hypotheses set against each other
a public persona against a private one, or a stated position against a revealed one
two eras of the same institution, product line or practice
a chapter-opening or chapter-closing card that frames a duality the narration will then argue
avoidWhen: Any quantity, score, count or measurement must appear
more or fewer than two subjects
the shot must survive a wide orbit
the two subjects cannot be supplied as clean transparent cutouts
an automated selector might mistake the word rows for data
items.caveats: THIS LAYOUT DISPLAYS NO DATA. It loads 180 generated observations and renders none of them, because showParticles is false. The five comparison rows are adjective pairs authored as placeholders, and the scene labels itself as concept copy on screen. Its name says 'Red Stage' but the surrounding world was later changed to pure black at the owner's request; the red comes only from the supplied photograph. As shipped it also hardcodes a specific real person's name, two of their photographs and eight lines of copy about them — an automated selector must not treat any of that as a variable slot without supplying its own replacements.

selection.selection_rule: Choose this layout when exactly two subjects must be set against each other qualitatively, when three clean images are available (two full-body cutouts and one wide environment plate), when every line of copy will be supplied, and when NO quantity needs to appear. items.title: Before-and-after rank-loss field
items.capacity: 3–12 entities; 1 rank delta per entity from a shared zero start; one optional hero expected to move little or not at all.
items.visualEncoding: Downward travel is proportional to rank places lost on one fixed linear axis. Marker size stays fixed so the movement alone carries the comparison.
examples: Most artists fall when their biggest record is removed while one remains stable
Products losing market rank after one feature is removed
Candidates dropping after one scoring category is excluded

The metric is a value change rather than an ordinal rank change

items.title: Five-layer single billboard
items.description: A five-layer editorial billboard with a dominant hero, reinforcing sidekick visual, short headline, replaceable background, and a foreground content section for supporting entities or data.
